title: Tesla Shows Off a Roadster That Can Lift Into the Air
summary:
Can a car fly? On Thursday night, Tesla and its CEO, Elon Musk, showed off the new Roadster 2 at an event in McGregor, Texas. The event took place at a rocket testing site run by SpaceX, another company Musk leads.

During the demonstration, the car burst into the air with a jerky puff of steam. At one point, it seemed to float several feet above Tesla's electric semi-truck. Tesla's head of vehicle engineering, Lars Moravy, said the "flying" is made possible by four thrusters. Tesla said the thrusters are powered by compressed gas stored in the car. Musk said the same technology will push the car down toward the road so it can take corners very quickly.

Tesla executives said the car could speed up from 0 to 60 miles per hour in one second. Moravy said the final version would "hopefully" reach up to 230 miles per hour. Musk said, "This is not necessarily a safety-optimized car." Wired noted that the car is likely to get attention from government safety regulators.

Tesla says it will start making the Roadster 2 in 2028. Fans have waited a long time. The car was first announced in 2017, and Tesla originally promised it would ship in 2020. Wired pointed out that many Tesla products have missed their planned release dates in the past. Tesla did not say how much the new car will cost.

The company says there will be three versions: a two-seat road version without thrusters, a "race ready" version, and a one-seat "air ready" version.

The unveiling comes at a tricky time for electric cars. Wired reports that electric car sales have stalled in the United States but are booming in some other parts of the world.
why_it_matters: Bold new vehicle designs show how engineers test new ideas, but they also raise questions about safety rules and whether promises will be kept.
